proposals.before: Song Taizuo 1: he became magistrate of Anji and won repute for strict, capable rule.
proposals.after: Song Taiyu 1: he became magistrate of Anji and won repute for strict, capable rule.
proposals.reason: 泰豫 is the Taiyu reign of Liu Song; Taizuo is a mistranslation of the reign name.

proposals.before: In the first year of Taizuo of Song, he was made magistrate of Anji and gained a name for stern competence.
proposals.after: In the first year of Taiyu of Song, he was made magistrate of Anji and gained a name for stern competence.
proposals.reason: 泰豫 is Taiyu, not Taizuo; the literal English should match the reign name in the Chinese.

proposals.before: the second year of Jianyuan: he bore the staff, supervised Ying and Yiyang in Sizhou, became champion general and inspector of Ying, and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan: he bore the staff, supervised Ying and Yiyang in Sizhou, became champion general and inspector of Ying, and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English sentence is missing an initial capital and reads as a sentence fragment.

proposals.before: In the fifth year he took the staff, supervised Xiyang in Ying and Runan in Si, became right general and inspector of Yu.
proposals.after: In the fifth year he took the staff, supervised Yuzhou together with Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, became right general and inspector of Yu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 監豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事 includes 豫州 in the supervision clause; the idiomatic English omits Yuzhou from that supervision.

proposals.before: Day wuzi: Bao Juan was made crown prince; every man who had become a father gained one rank; filial sons, worthy grandsons, righteous men, and faithful widows were sought out, praised, and rewarded.
proposals.after: Day wuzi: Bao Juan was made crown prince; every man who stood as heir to his father gained one rank; filial sons, worthy grandsons, righteous men, and faithful widows were sought out, praised, and rewarded.
proposals.reason: 爲父後者 means agnatic heirs succeeding their fathers, not men who had become fathers.

proposals.before: Day wuzi: the crown prince Bao Juan was established; all who had become fathers received one rank; filial sons, obedient grandsons, men of righteousness, and chaste wives were broadly singled out, commended, and promoted.
proposals.after: Day wuzi: the crown prince Bao Juan was established; all who were heirs to their fathers received one rank; filial sons, obedient grandsons, men of righteousness, and chaste wives were broadly singled out, commended, and promoted.
proposals.reason: 爲父後者 is 'heirs/successors to their fathers,' not 'those who had become fathers.'

proposals.before: Eleventh month, day guiyou: Staff Clerk of the West Central Corps Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Administrator of Jinshou Wang Hongfan was made Inspector of Qing and Ji; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan additionally led the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.
proposals.after: Eleventh month, day guiyou: Staff Clerk of the West Central Corps Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Administrator of Jinshou Wang Hongfan was made Inspector of Qing and Ji; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan additionally held the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.
proposals.reason: 領太子少傅 means concurrently held that office; 'led' mistranslates 領.

proposals.before: Mian, marquis of Anlu, was posthumously raised to prince of Anlu.
proposals.after: Mian, Marquis Zhao of Anlu, was posthumously raised to prince of Anlu.
proposals.reason: 安陸昭侯 includes the posthumous epithet 昭 omitted in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: A second edict said: "Food is the people's heaven—the Book of Ji sets its meaning high; silkworms are the root of living—the canon of Xuan gives their teaching weight.
proposals.after: A second edict said: "Food is the people's heaven—the Ji records set its meaning high; silkworms are the root of living—the canon of Xuan gives their teaching weight.
proposals.reason: 姬載 refers to the records/writings associated with the Ji (Zhou), not a discrete work titled "Book of Ji"; the invented book title over-specifies the allusion.

proposals.before: Seventh month of autumn, day xinwei: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, right general, took South Xu.
proposals.after: Seventh month of autumn, day xinwei: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, right general, was made inspector of South Xu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 爲南徐州刺史 is an appointment as inspector; "took South Xu" omits the office and can be read as conquest rather than posting.

proposals.before: Eighth month, day dingwei: Prince Bao Yuan of Luling, right guards general, took South Yan.
proposals.after: Eighth month, day dingwei: Prince Bao Yuan of Luling, right guards general, was made inspector of South Yan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 爲南兖州刺史 is an appointment as inspector; "took South Yan" omits the office and can be read as conquest rather than posting.

proposals.before: Third year, spring, first month, day dingmao: Yang Chongzu, son of Yang Gui of Yinping, was made inspector of Sha and enfeoffed as prince of Yinping.
proposals.after: Third year, spring, first month, day dingmao: Yang Chongzu, son of Yang Gui, Prince of Yinping, was made inspector of Sha and enfeoffed as prince of Yinping.
proposals.reason: 陰平王楊炅 names the father as Prince of Yinping; 'of Yinping' understates the princely title already explicit in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Fifth month, day jisi: Xiao Yi, suppressing-the-barbarians general, took Yi; Yin Guangzong, vanguard general, took Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, newly relieved of Ning, was again made inspector of Ning.
proposals.after: Fifth month, day jisi: Xiao Yi, suppressing-the-barbarians general, took Yi; Yin Guangzong, vanguard general, took Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, previously newly appointed inspector of Ning, was again made inspector of Ning.
proposals.reason: 前新除 means previously newly appointed to the office, not relieved from it; 新除 is the standard term for a fresh appointment.

proposals.before: Fifth month, day jisi: Suppressing-the-Barbarians General Xiao Yi was made Inspector of Yi; Vanguard General Yin Guangzong was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, newly relieved as inspector of Ning, was again made Inspector of Ning.
proposals.after: Fifth month, day jisi: Suppressing-the-Barbarians General Xiao Yi was made Inspector of Yi; Vanguard General Yin Guangzong was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, previously newly appointed as Inspector of Ning, was again made Inspector of Ning.
proposals.reason: 前新除寧州刺史 means he had lately been appointed Inspector of Ning, not that he was relieved of that post.

proposals.before: Second month, day guichou: Xiao Hui, left guards general on leave, bore the staff and marched to relieve Shouyang.
proposals.after: Second month, day guichou: Xiao Huixiu, left guards general, bore the staff of authority and marched to relieve Shouyang.
proposals.reason: 蕭惠休 is the personal name; 假節 means bearing the staff of authority, not on leave.

proposals.before: Second month, day guichou: Left Guards General Xiao Hui on leave of absence bore the staff and went to aid Shouyang.
proposals.after: Second month, day guichou: Left Guards General Xiao Huixiu, bearing the staff of authority, went to aid Shouyang.
proposals.reason: 蕭惠休 is the personal name; 假節 is the staff-authority formula, not leave of absence.

proposals.before: Xiao Yingke, rear army chief clerk, took South Yan.
proposals.after: Xiao Yingzhou, rear army chief clerk, took South Yan.
proposals.reason: 蕭穎胄 is Xiao Yingzhou; Yingke misreads 胄.

proposals.before: Rear Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yingke was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
proposals.after: Rear Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
proposals.reason: 蕭穎胄 is Xiao Yingzhou; Yingke misreads 胄.

proposals.before: Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Hui on leave, and Cui Huijing."
proposals.after: Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huixiu, and Cui Huijing."
proposals.reason: 蕭惠休 is the personal name Huixiu, not Hui on leave.

proposals.after: Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huixiu, and Cui Huijing."

proposals.before: Shamans and spirit-mediums said: "The headwaters of Rear Lake pass through the palace grounds, causing the emperor's illness.」
proposals.after: Shamans and spirit-mediums said: "The headwaters of Rear Lake pass through the palace grounds, causing the emperor's illness."
proposals.reason: Closing quotation uses a Chinese corner bracket instead of an English quote mark.

proposals.after: Attendants reported: "If the Grand Provisioner lacked this water it could not operate."
proposals.reason: Closing quotation uses a Chinese corner bracket instead of an English quote mark.

proposals.before: He cast off kinsmen of the shared patrimony before they cast him off;
proposals.after: He cast off first the kinsmen who shared the same inheritance, while power was still his;
proposals.reason: Chinese 在我而先棄 means he abandoned shared-patrimony kin first while he held power; the idiomatic added a reciprocal cast-off by them that the source does not state.

proposals.before: Dread and doubt ran deep; every glance seemed an outsider's plot. He wept and killed—and no man called it justice. If a throne is held by fear alone, what night is free of shame?
proposals.after: Suspicion and timidity ran deep; mistrust seemed to come from without. He wept as he carried out executions—not called a righteous act; if one seeks only safety in the affair, how can there be no inner shame?
proposals.reason: The idiomatic invents throne-by-fear and sleepless shame imagery; the Chinese asks whether seeking only safety can be free of inner shame, closer to the literal.

decisions.reason: s0005 has 宋泰豫元年; 泰豫 is the Liu Song reign name Taiyu, so Taizuo is a clear mistranslation and Song Taiyu 1 restores the correct era.
The literal of s0005 likewise renders 泰豫 as Taizuo; Taiyu matches the Chinese reign name without other changes.
The idiomatic of s0011 begins with lowercase “the,” which is not a grammatical sentence start; adding “In” and capitalizing fixes a real error while leaving the rest of the wording intact.
s0019’s 監豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事 includes 豫州 in the supervision scope; the idiomatic had omitted Yuzhou from that clause while keeping only inspector of Yu, and the proposed wording restores it.

decisions.reason: 賜天下爲父後者爵一級 uses 爲父後者 for agnatic heirs who stand as successors to their fathers, not men who had become fathers; the proposed idiomatic corrects that semantic error.
The same 爲父後者 in the literal of s0064 was mistranslated as those who had become fathers; “heirs to their fathers” restores the technical sense.

decisions.reason: 尚書令王晏領太子少傅 uses 領 for concurrent tenure of the junior-tutor office; “led” misreads that formula, and “held” is accurate.
追贈安陸昭侯緬爲安陸王 includes the posthumous epithet 昭; omitting it from the idiomatic drops part of the Chinese title, and Marquis Zhao of Anlu restores it.
義高姬載 alludes to Ji (Zhou) records/writings parallel to 軒經, not a discrete titled “Book of Ji”; “the Ji records” removes the invented book title.
以…爲南徐州刺史 is an appointment as inspector; “took South Xu” drops 刺史 and can read as conquest, while “was made inspector of South Xu” matches the Chinese.
爲南兖州刺史 likewise marks an inspector appointment; replacing “took South Yan” with “was made inspector of South Yan” restores the office.
陰平王楊炅 titles the father Prince of Yinping; “Yang Gui of Yinping” understates 王, and “Yang Gui, Prince of Yinping” restores the rank.
前新除寧州刺史 uses 新除 for a prior fresh appointment, not relief from office; “previously newly appointed inspector of Ning” corrects the false “relieved.”
The literal of s0131 makes the same error on 前新除; “previously newly appointed as Inspector of Ning” matches the bureaucratic formula.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前新除寧州刺史李慶宗爲寧州刺史

decisions.reason: 遣左衛將軍蕭惠休假節援壽陽 parses as Xiao Huixiu plus 假節 (staff of authority), not Xiao Hui on leave; the proposed idiomatic fixes both the name and the office formula.
The literal likewise splits 蕭惠休 and misreads 假節 as leave; Xiao Huixiu bearing the staff of authority restores the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 左衛將軍蕭惠休假節援壽陽

decisions.reason: 蕭穎胄 is Xiao Yingzhou; Yingke misreads 胄, and the proposed name correction is accurate.
The literal of s0176 has the same Yingke error for 蕭穎胄; Xiao Yingzhou is the correct romanization.
心膂之任可委…蕭惠休… lists the personal name Huixiu with no leave formula; “Xiao Hui on leave” is a false parsing, and Xiao Huixiu is correct.
The literal of s0185 repeats the same misreading of 蕭惠休; replacing “Xiao Hui on leave” with Xiao Huixiu restores the name.
The English literal closes the quotation with a Chinese corner bracket 」 instead of "; swapping to an English closing quote is a real orthographic fix with no semantic change.
s0203’s literal likewise ends with 」 in the English field; an English closing quotation mark is the correct repair.

令同財之親，在我而先棄 means he cast off shared-patrimony kin first while power was still his; “before they cast him off” invents a reciprocal act absent from the Chinese, and the proposal removes that invention.
事苟求安，能無內愧？ asks whether seeking only safety can be free of inner shame; the idiomatic’s throne-by-fear and sleepless-night imagery is invented, and the proposed wording tracks the Chinese.
